newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures seen stable before U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures seen stable before U.S. data.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were higher but off the session peaks in late dealings on Tuesday as cash market 10-year yields remained below the psychologically important six percent level, traders said.
At 1530 GMT, DTB December Bund futures were up 26 basis points at 99.56 points in heavy trade as German trading volume topped 74,000 contracts.

Despite signs the market was ready for some profit-taking, traders said the market was still in a bullish mood and was gaining strength to break tough resistance at 99.70, with support coming from higher U.S. debt prices.
Firm dealings are expected ahead of the release on Wednesday at 1230 GMT of U.S. consumer price data for September, which a Reuter consensus survey expects to rise 0.3 percent month-on-month.
A firmer German share market and record gains on Wall Street also helped to underpin the market but traders said any profit-taking in share markets would not severely hurt Bunds.
"The debt market has not fully followed the share market higher in Germany, so we will not fully follow them lower," said one Frankfurt trader.
